title: hymns to Agni, Indra, Ushas, Varuna
hook: "where is he?" some ask. "he is not," some say. a hymn to Indra quotes its doubters out loud

segments.voice: Yesterday, hymns to Agni: the fire in the house, asked to be easy to approach, as a father to his son.
screen: `EASY TO REACH, AS A FATHER TO A SON.`

segments.voice: "Where is he?" people ask. "He isn't real," others answer. It could be an argument at a dinner table this week. It's a line from a hymn in the Rig Veda, book two, and the god being doubted is Indra: the storm, the warrior, the one who breaks the dam and lets the rivers run. The hymn could have left the doubters out. Instead it quotes them, right in the middle of the praise. Today: the second voice, Indra.
screen: `"WHERE IS HE?"` → `"HE ISN'T REAL."` → `A HYMN THAT QUOTES ITS DOUBTERS.`

segments.voice: Indra is the mighty one of the Rig Veda's storms. In its stories he fights Vritra, a serpent coiled around the waters, holding them back, and when Indra strikes him down, the rivers pour free. He drinks soma, rides with the storm, and stands with those who call on him. Book two, hymn twelve, praises him in a shape you can hear even in paraphrase. Verse after verse tells something he did: he steadied the shaking earth, spread out the sky, killed the serpent and set the rivers flowing. And verse after verse ends the same way. Sa janasa indrah. He, O people, is Indra. Then, in the fifth verse, the hymn turns. In paraphrase: the terrible one, about whom they ask, where is he? About whom they say, he is not. The singer's answer isn't an argument. It's an invitation: put your trust in him. He, O people, is Indra. A hymn of praise names, out loud, the people who don't believe in the god it praises. It doesn't hide the question or pretend nobody asks it. It lets the question stand, answers it with trust, and goes on singing. Earlier on this path the Nasadiya Sukta asked who really knows how the world began. Here, a hymn to the god of the storm makes room for someone saying he isn't there at all.
screen: `INDRA FREES THE WATERS.` · `"HE, O PEOPLE, IS INDRA."` · `"WHERE IS HE?" "HE IS NOT."` · `THE QUESTION STAYS IN THE HYMN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you're unsure of, about life, faith, a person or yourself, and let it be asked without arguing or settling it. Beside it, find one thing you do trust, even something small: the floor holding you, the breath coming back, someone who has shown up for you. Hold both, and if you pray, offer both.
Hymns to Agni, and today, to Indra. In Rig Veda book two, hymn twelve, each verse ends, he, O people, is Indra, and one verse quotes those who say, he is not. Today's word.
Your line: hymns to Agni, Indra, Ushas, Varuna. A hymn can hold a doubt and still sing. Go gently.

chat.says: Do the old hymns ever admit some people doubted the gods?
options: Yes: a hymn to Indra quotes them, where is he? he is not, and answers with trust.
No, the hymns only praise; doubt shows up much later, in other books.
Yes, and the hymn mocks the doubters, then curses them with a storm.
